While the idea of UBI as an "investment in human potential" is appealing, it ignores the harsh reality that such a policy would require diverting resources from critical areas that directly impact human well-being. If governments are forced to fund UBI through higher taxes or cuts to public services, the very people who need healthcare, education, and infrastructure the most will suffer. UBI assumes that a universal payment will automatically lead to better outcomes, but it fails to address the structural inequalities that exist within societies. For example, a basic income may help someone afford food, but it won’t provide access to quality healthcare or job training. Moreover, UBI treats all individuals as if they have the same needs and opportunities, which is far from the truth. A more targeted, needs-based approach to social support would be far more effective and equitable than a one-size-fits-all solution like UBI.
